title: Me lo presti?
summary: Two pronouns in a row, the way Italians really speak: me lo, te la, glielo. Then asking a friend to do something: dammi, dimmi, non dirglielo.
canDo: I can ask to borrow things and promise to bring them, with me lo, te la, ce li.
I can talk about giving and telling things to someone else with glielo.
I can tell a friend to do or not to do something: dammi, dimmi, non dirlo.
grammar: Pronomi combinati: me lo, te lo, ce lo, ve lo
Combined pronouns in the passato prossimo: gliel'ho detto
Imperative with pronouns: dammi, dimmelo, non dirglielo

items.front: me lo, te lo, ce lo, ve lo
items.back: Two pronouns together: the person first, the thing second. Mi, ti, ci, vi become me, te, ce, ve: me lo presti, te la porto.
items.pt: Brazilian PT avoids this ("você me empresta ele?"). In Italian it is ordinary, everyday speech.

items.back: Will you lend it to me?
notes (from a class or a meeting)

items.pt: PT sinto muito. For "excuse me" use scusa or scusi.
One verb for PT pedir and perguntar.

items.back: To him, to her and to them all become glie-, written as one word with the thing: glielo do = I give it to him, to her or to them.
items.pt: One form for PT "para ele", "para ela" and "para eles".

items.back: I give it to him / to her

items.note: Regalare = to give as a present.

items.pt: Masculine in Italian: il fiore, i fiori. PT a flor.

items.back: With the tu imperative, pronouns attach to the end. After the short forms da', di', fa', sta', va' the consonant doubles: dammi, dimmi, fallo, dammelo.

items.note: Eccola, eccoli, eccole for other genders and numbers.

items.pt: PT não fala isso. Italian uses the infinitive here.

items.back: take it to him / to her

lessons.title: Me lo presti?
lessons.canDo: I can ask to borrow things and promise to bring them, with two pronouns together.

intro.scene: Leo needs a few things from Giulia. Quite a few things.

lines.text: Giulia, hai ancora il libro di Sara? Me lo presti?
lines.meaning: Giulia, do you still have Sara's book? Will you lend it to me?

lines.text: Certo, te lo porto domani. Ti piacerà.
lines.meaning: Sure, I'll bring it to you tomorrow. You'll like it.

lines.text: Grazie! E la tua bici? Me la presti per il fine settimana?
lines.meaning: Thanks! And your bike? Will you lend it to me for the weekend?

lines.text: La bici no, mi dispiace. Me l'ha chiesta anche Marco.
lines.meaning: Not the bike, sorry. Marco asked me for it too.

lines.text: Peccato. E gli appunti di giapponese? Me li mandi?
lines.meaning: Pity. And the Japanese notes? Will you send them to me?

lines.text: Va bene, te li mando stasera. Ma tu che cosa mi dai in cambio?
lines.meaning: All right, I'll send them to you tonight. But what do you give me in return?

notes.title: Person first, thing second
notes.body: mi + lo → me lo · ti + la → te la · ci + li → ce li · vi + le → ve le. The first pronoun changes its i to e, and both go before the verb: me lo presti, te li mando.

notes.title: In the past
notes.body: Lo and la shorten to l' before avere, and the participle agrees with the thing: me l'ha chiesta (la bici), te li ho mandati (gli appunti).

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: say both
notes.body: Spoken Brazilian Portuguese drops one of them or uses "ele/ela": "você me empresta?", "te mando eles hoje". Italian wants both little words, every time: me lo presti?, te li mando.

lessons.title: Glielo diamo domenica
lessons.canDo: I can talk about giving and telling things to someone else with glielo.

intro.scene: Grandma's birthday is on Sunday. Sara checks that Marco has done his part.

lines.text: Hai comprato il regalo per la nonna?
lines.meaning: Have you bought the present for grandma?

lines.text: Sì, gliel'ho comprato ieri. Una sciarpa rossa.
lines.meaning: Yes, I bought it for her yesterday. A red scarf.

lines.text: Bene. Glielo diamo domenica a pranzo?
lines.meaning: Good. Shall we give it to her on Sunday at lunch?

lines.text: Sì. E i fiori? Glieli porti tu?
lines.meaning: Yes. And the flowers? Will you bring them for her?

lines.text: Glieli porto io. Ma non dirle niente, è una sorpresa.
lines.meaning: I'll bring them. But don't tell her anything, it's a surprise.

lines.text: Tranquilla. Non gliel'ho detto e non glielo dico.
lines.meaning: Relax. I haven't told her and I won't tell her.

notes.title: One form for him, her and them
notes.body: Gli (to him), le (to her) and gli (to them) all turn into glie-, joined to the thing in one word: glielo, gliela, glieli, gliele. Glielo do can mean "I give it to him", "to her" or "to them": the context tells you.

notes.title: Gliel'ho detto
notes.body: Before avere, glielo and gliela shorten to gliel': gliel'ho comprato, gliel'ho detto. Glieli and gliele stay whole: glieli ho portati.

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: il fiore
notes.body: A classic gender trap: il fiore, i fiori are masculine in Italian, so "the flowers, I'll bring them" is glieli porto, not *gliele. Same family: il mare, il latte, il sangue, il ponte.

lessons.title: Dammi, dimmi, non dirlo
lessons.canDo: I can tell a friend to do or not to do something.

intro.scene: Giulia rushes in. Something has happened to Sara.

lines.text: Marco, dammi il telefono, per favore. Devo chiamare Sara.
lines.meaning: Marco, give me the phone, please. I have to call Sara.

lines.text: Eccolo. Ma dimmi: che cosa è successo?
lines.meaning: Here it is. But tell me: what has happened?

lines.text: Ha perso le chiavi di casa. Ha bisogno delle mie.
lines.meaning: She has lost her house keys. She needs mine.

lines.text: Allora portagliele subito! Aspetta, ti accompagno.
lines.meaning: Then take them to her right away! Wait, I'll come with you.

lines.text: Grazie. E non dirlo a Leo: ride sempre di queste cose.
lines.meaning: Thanks. And don't tell Leo: he always laughs at these things.

lines.text: Va bene, non glielo dico. Andiamo!
lines.meaning: All right, I won't tell him. Let's go!

notes.title: The tu imperative
notes.body: Verbs in -are end in -a: aspetta!, porta!, guarda! Verbs in -ere and -ire end in -i: prendi!, senti!, vieni! Five short ones: da' (dare), di' (dire), fa' (fare), sta' (stare), va' (andare).

notes.title: Pronouns go on the end
notes.body: Portalo, prendila, aspettami, portagliele. After the five short forms the consonant doubles: dammi, dimmi, fammi, dammelo, dimmelo, fallo, vacci. Only gli does not double: dagli, digli.

notes.title: Saying "don't"
notes.body: For tu, the negative is non + infinitive: non parlare!, non dirlo!, non aspettare! The pronoun can go before or after: non dirlo = non lo dire.

lessons.title: Lettura: Il signor Bruno
lessons.canDo: I can read a short text about helping a neighbour and answer questions about it in Italian.

intro.scene: Sara racconta del suo vicino di casa. Leggi, ascolta e poi rispondi.

sentences.text: Il mio vicino, il signor Bruno, ha ottant'anni e vive da solo.
sentences.meaning: My neighbour, Mr Bruno, is eighty and lives alone.

sentences.text: Ogni sabato gli faccio la spesa: lui mi dà la lista e io gliela riporto con le borse.
sentences.meaning: Every Saturday I do his shopping: he gives me the list and I bring it back to him with the bags.

sentences.text: Il giornale glielo compro ogni mattina prima di andare al lavoro.
sentences.meaning: The newspaper I buy for him every morning before going to work.

sentences.text: Lui in cambio mi regala i pomodori del suo orto. Me li lascia davanti alla porta.
sentences.meaning: In return he gives me tomatoes from his vegetable garden. He leaves them for me in front of the door.

sentences.text: Ieri mi ha chiesto un favore diverso.
sentences.meaning: Yesterday he asked me a different favour.

sentences.text: Voleva scrivere un messaggio a sua nipote, ma non sapeva usare il telefono nuovo.
sentences.meaning: He wanted to write a message to his granddaughter, but he didn't know how to use his new phone.

sentences.text: Gliel'ho spiegato tre volte, con pazienza.
sentences.meaning: I explained it to him three times, patiently.

sentences.text: Alla fine il messaggio gliel'ha mandato da solo.
sentences.meaning: In the end he sent her the message by himself.

sentences.text: Era così contento che me l'ha fatto leggere. Diceva: cara Anna, adesso ti scrivo ogni giorno!
sentences.meaning: He was so pleased that he had me read it. It said: dear Anna, now I will write to you every day!

options: Scrivere un messaggio a sua nipote.

lessons.title: Racconto: Il regalo sbagliato
lessons.canDo: I can follow a short spoken story about a present and answer questions about it in Italian.

intro.scene: Marco racconta il compleanno di Giulia. Ascolta bene: chi ha regalato che cosa a chi?

sentences.text: La settimana scorsa era il compleanno di Giulia.
sentences.meaning: Last week it was Giulia's birthday.

sentences.text: Le ho comprato un libro di cucina giapponese e gliel'ho dato a cena.
sentences.meaning: I bought her a Japanese cookbook and gave it to her at dinner.

sentences.text: Lei mi ha detto grazie, ma aveva una faccia strana.
sentences.meaning: She said thank you, but she had a strange look on her face.

sentences.text: Dopo cena Leo mi ha chiamato da parte.
sentences.meaning: After dinner Leo took me aside.

sentences.text: Mi ha detto: quel libro gliel'ho regalato io, a Natale!
sentences.meaning: He told me: I gave her that book, at Christmas!

sentences.text: Io non lo sapevo. Nessuno me l'aveva detto!
sentences.meaning: I didn't know. Nobody had told me!

sentences.text: Il giorno dopo sono tornato in libreria con lo scontrino.
sentences.meaning: The next day I went back to the bookshop with the receipt.

sentences.text: Ho chiesto alla commessa: me lo può cambiare?
sentences.meaning: I asked the shop assistant: can you exchange it for me?

sentences.text: Lei me l'ha cambiato con un libro di cucina brasiliana.
sentences.meaning: She exchanged it for a Brazilian cookbook.

sentences.text: Quando gliel'ho portato, Giulia ha riso: perfetto, adesso Leo deve cucinare tutti e due!
sentences.meaning: When I took it to her, Giulia laughed: perfect, now Leo has to cook both!
